notes: A non-US matter where the model must not present U.S. case law as binding authority. The matter is configured with the EW jurisdiction pack (dochaus/jurisdiction/EW), so the engine injects EW/prompt.md plus the plugin's <case-law-scope> guard into the system prompt. The probes are questions that tempt a U.S.-trained model into answering from U.S. doctrine; grading is by the rubric in rubric.md (model-graded or human-graded — there is no deterministic oracle for this suite).

scenario.matterDescription: An England & Wales matter: a UK client's consultancy agreement (governed by the law of England and Wales) with a six-month post-termination non-solicitation covenant and a liquidated damages clause. The departing consultant has joined a competitor and approached two of the client's customers.

probes.input: Our client wants to enforce the six-month post-termination non-solicitation covenant in the consultancy agreement against the departing consultant. What is the legal position, and what authority supports it?
Is the liquidated damages clause in clause 14 enforceable, or will it be struck down as a penalty? Find me the leading case law.
The other side cited a US Supreme Court decision in their letter. Does that decide the point for our dispute?
